title: Opening the account: documents, fees, signers

sources.claim: The SBA lists the launch steps (choose a structure, register, get federal and state tax IDs, apply for licenses and permits, open a business bank account, get insurance) as a general guide.

sections.skill: Prepare documents and compare business account fees and signers

questions.prompt: What is a signer on a bank account?

choices.text: The bank employee who opened the account
A customer who pays the business by check
A person allowed to use the account
The state office that approved the LLC

questions.correct_answer: A person allowed to use the account
questions.intro: Banks set their own rules, but opening a business account usually requires: the business's formation papers (for an LLC or corporation), the EIN (or an SSN for some sole proprietors), a DBA certificate if using a trade name, and personal ID for each signer. A SIGNER is a person allowed to use the account. Compare accounts: monthly fees, minimum balance needed to avoid fees, transaction limits, cash deposit fees and online tools. Read the fee schedule before choosing; a "free" account may have conditions.

questions.prompt: What happens if you arrive without the right papers?
questions.intro: Opening a business account is like checking in for a flight: you bring the right papers or you get sent back. Bring proof the business exists (formation papers or a DBA certificate), the tax ID (EIN), and a photo ID for each person who will use the account. Then, like comparing airline baggage fees, compare the account's fees before you choose.
